note: Read-only tasks on a large real codebase (rtk: ~100k lines of Rust, 1,700 commits). Each task is phrased so the natural path produces a large tool output: whole-file Reads, wide greps, git history and diffs, a test run. `check` is a regex the final answer must match.

tasks.name: main-rs-overview
tasks.prompt: Read src/main.rs in full and give a structured overview: every top-level `mod` declaration, the name of the CLI struct, the enum that holds the subcommands, and the first 12 variants of that enum in order. Do not guess; read the file.

tasks.name: git-rs-run-fns
tasks.prompt: Read src/cmds/git/git.rs and list every function whose name starts with `run_`, in file order, with its starting line number. Then say in one sentence what `compact_diff` does with context lines.

tasks.name: history-hotspots
tasks.prompt: Using `git log --stat -60`, tell me which 5 files changed most often in the last 60 commits, with counts, and the subject line of the most recent commit that touched the top file.

tasks.name: recent-diff-review
tasks.prompt: Show `git diff HEAD~8 HEAD` and review it: list the files changed with insertions/deletions, name the single change you consider riskiest, and quote the one changed line that justifies it.

tasks.name: grep-unwrap-audit
tasks.prompt: Search the whole src/ tree for `.unwrap()` calls outside `#[cfg(test)]` modules. Report the 5 files with the most occurrences and their counts, and one example line from the top file with its line number.
